name: Snake Restaurants
desc: The suburb of Le Mat (aka Snake Village) has numerous restaurants specializing in cobra foodstuffs. Live cobras are stored on the premises much the same way one would find live lobsters at a Western seafood restaurant. I

name: Bánh Mì Dân Tổ
desc: The sandwich is very delicious and crispy. Pretty crowded. You can also eat there at 3am and it will feel delicious.

name: Bun Cha Ta Hanoi
desc: Highly recommended if you are looking for authentic North Vietnamese Bun Cha. The food is great, bursting with flavour. Very cosy place.

name: Bánh Mì 25
desc: Vietnamese Sandwiches. This is a good restaurant for a quick bite to eat near Dong Xuan Market. Lovely place and mouth watering food.

name: Little Hanoi Restaurant
desc: Simple Vietnamese home-cooked food. Also amazing vegan food. The fried tofu in tomato sauce and grilled eggplant are delicious. Also a cute date spot.

name: Banh Mi Hoi An
desc: Vietnamese Sandwiches. This place is open from early morning and serves great bahn mi. Nice staff with good English skills.

name: Quán Cơm Bình Dân
desc: Inexpensive, home-cooked Vietnamese meals. Delicious and nutritious rice, clean restaurant.

name: Bún Chả Đắc Kim

name: Pho 10 Ly Quoc Su
desc: Serve delicious beef rice noodle, fried bread stick is crispy and delicious. The place is so clean and nice. All of the soups and sides include beef (bo), so this isn't for vegetarians.

name: Pho Tu Lun (Au Trieu)
desc: Many pho varieties. Store is only open in the morning. Locals crowd the place, so you know it must be good.

name: Com Chay Nang Tam Vegetarian Restaurant
desc: This excellent restaurant is a good vegetarian option, and will please both vegetarians and non-vegetarians with its wide range of innovative dishes, which include fake meat dishes. Restaurant is comfortable with good am

name: Au Lac Vegetarian Restaurant
desc: Typical local vegetarian restaurant like you'll find everywhere in Vietnam except Hanoi, a little off the beaten track in an atmospheric alleyway.

name: Huyen Huong Restaurant
desc: Choose from a wide variety of seafood dishes (many of which are swimming around in tanks) and other Vietnamese specialities. Friendly staff complements the tasty food.

name: Kaiser Kaffee Restaurant
desc: Interesting little place which has excellent Vietnamese and Western food.

name: Little Hanoi
desc: Upscale cafe serving mainly Westerners in a pleasantly lit restaurant.

name: Mediterraneo
desc: Authentic Italian food, probably the best you'll get in Hanoi. Prices are steep and portions small.

name: Moka Café
desc: Excellent selection of Western and Vietnamese food served in a coffee shop environment.

name: Pepperoni's

name: 01 -wan- Tantan Ramen
desc: Two-floor ramen shop owned by a Japanese chef, specialising in excellent tantanmen with creamy, Sichuan-inspired "numbing spicy" mala broth.

name: Madam Tu Hong
desc: Restaurant specialising in cha ca (Hanoi-style turmeric-and-dill grilled fish cooked at the table), set in a restored old house once belonging to Madam Tu Hong, a 19th-century Vietnamese businesswoman.

name: Dalcheeni

price: Tasting menu only: lunch from 1,400K don
desc: Go here for a purely Vietnamese fine dining experience, without Gia's more Western-leaning influences. High-quality, farm-to-table ingredients obtained from across the north. Closed on weekends; reservations essential.

name: JW Café
addr: 8 Đỗ Đức Dục St., Mễ Trì, Nam Từ Liêm

name: Lý Club
desc: Top-notch Vietnamese and European cuisine in a French colonial mansion. On the expensive side for Hanoi, but the atmosphere and good quality of food make up for it. A pianist alternates with piped music.

name: Pane e Vino Italian Restaurant and Wine Shop

name: Stellar Steakhouse
addr: 62nd Floor, Keangnam Hanoi Landmark Tower, Mễ Trì, Nam Từ Liêm

addr: 70 Phan Kế Bính, Cống Vị, Ba Đình

name: T.U.N.G Dining
desc: Hanoi's first high-end tasting menu experience. Cozy second-floor dining room, serving inventive and technically accomplished Modern Scandinavian cuisine. Reservations essential.

name: Kem Tràng Tiền
desc: Popular spot for ice cream on a hot day. Beware of motorbikes when entering the establishment, since it is sort of a drive-thru/drive-in ice cream shop. Recommended is the local cóm or đậu xanh flavours.

name: Furbrew
desc: Danish-owned, Danish-style craft brewery.

name: Green Lake (Ho Guom Xanh)

name: Standing Bar
desc: Wide variety of Vietnamese craft beer, mostly from the south, but with a limited selection from the local Long Bien brewery. Despite the name, seats are available upstairs.

desc: Several locations across the city, although the most central is probably the one at 54 Ma May. Serves various coffees, chocolates and teas including their speciality coconut coffee smoothie (around 45,000 dong). Popular

name: Mien Man Cafe
desc: Multi-storey art-themed cafe directly behind St. Joseph's Cathedral, serving specialty coffee and house-made syrups. Upper-floor balcony tables overlook the cathedral; non-coffee options available.
